about.heading: Who am I?
about.p1: My name is André Hommrich. I'm {age} years old and live in the Westerwald region of Germany. What drives me most is the question of why things work the way they do. I rarely settle for an answer before I have truly understood it.
about.p2: I started out in the trades, as an electronics technician for energy and building technology. Even then I always wanted to understand what was behind a task rather than just work through it. In software development, that habit of asking questions has become my most important tool. Here it pays off to fully grasp a problem before solving it.
about.p3: Today I work full-time as a software developer on real-world projects. Alongside that, I build websites for smaller companies, local businesses and clubs, as well as private applications for myself, from the first idea to running them in production. What drives me is always the same standard: understand before you build, and build to last.

currently.heading: What I'm working on
currently.p1: As a full-stack web developer, I take an application from the first plan all the way into day-to-day operation. Much of what I build, I also run myself afterwards. That's why, even while developing, I make sure it will run reliably later on. For example, I check whether a backup can actually be restored when it matters, and I treat data protection as a fixed part of the technology, not as something you add at the end.
currently.p2: Over my years as a developer, I've noticed how well the job suits me: I'm constantly learning, and I get to work through problems that the first obvious solution doesn't settle. That's what I enjoy most about the work.

tech.heading: What I work with
tech.p1: My focus is back-end development with PHP, professionally with Symfony and privately with Laravel. On the front end I mainly work with Vue.js, React and TypeScript, and for styling with Tailwind CSS and Bootstrap. For mobile applications I bring experience with React Native. That way I build a project myself, from the database model to the interface. I use AI tools like Claude Code deliberately. They take routine work off my hands and make me faster. The decisions and the understanding stay with me.
tech.p2: Docker, Git, CI/CD pipelines and databases with MySQL or MariaDB are part of my daily work. When I look after several websites, they run on a shared, self-hosted infrastructure, so I can handle maintenance and operation in one place instead of patching each one separately. I look at new frameworks and tools once they genuinely help with real tasks, not because they happen to be new.
tech.disclaimer: A selection of tools and technologies I use regularly.

frontend.title: Website (front end)
frontend.text: Everything you see and click in the browser: text, images, buttons and forms. The visible surface of the application. It's loaded from the web and runs directly in the browser, with no installation.

mobile.title: App (mobile)
mobile.text: Installed directly on the phone: touch controls, small screens, access to camera, GPS and sensors. Works even without internet and stays within reach on the home screen.

backend.title: Back end (engine room)
backend.text: The invisible engine. This is where things are calculated, checked and decided, such as logins, permissions and workflows. On top of that come background jobs like emails or interfaces. Users never see it, but nothing runs without it.

db.title: Database (archive)
db.text: The safe place where all data lives permanently: accounts, content and settings. At the next login everything is there again, even after a restart, an update or from another device.

ops.title: Deployment, hosting & versioning
ops.text: It sits above everything: code is versioned (roll back to earlier states at any time), run on servers (hosting) and put live without downtime (deployment). That keeps the system reachable and open to change.

eventplaner.description: A wedding and event planner I built entirely myself as a progressive web app, with a native companion app for guests (React Native / Expo) connected to the Laravel back end via a JSON API. Guests authenticate by QR code without a password; the personal event hub offers a photo gallery with upload, a photo game with a delta-based task model, a drinking game with physiologically motivated scoring and a token-secured projector slideshow. The back end is covered by around 200 automated Pest tests, with a three-stage deploy process (develop → staging → production) and a CI guard against compose drift. Live at eveplan.de.

portfolio.description: A personal portfolio website with no external runtime dependencies — no CDN, no tracking, no analytics. Tech-icon section with its own requestAnimationFrame loop, physics model and pointer-flee behaviour. Hero section as a rotated CSS grid. Deployed via Docker and Coolify. Live at hommri.ch.

grapeminds.description: A web application with a companion smartphone app for managing wine stocks and providing information about the available wines. As a front-end developer, I built new features, optimised existing components and refactored the code base. Working independently made the development process more efficient and steadily improved the quality of the application.

crm.description: Extending the internal CRM with a forecast feature that gives sales staff an overview of employees and freelancers — including project duration, departure dates and revenue/profit forecasts with targets and visual feedback. Absences are automatically taken into account in revenue and profit calculations. In addition, a system-wide activity log that documents every change in a fully traceable way.

platform.description: Modernising the company website of the training company and extending it with an employee and time-management platform. Internal and external staff manage their profiles, record working hours and get an overall overview of current hours and project timelines.

elade.description: A monitoring system for the wall boxes at the office location, running on a Raspberry Pi at the training company. Real-time capture of charging data, power consumption, electricity prices and grid load. Calculation of charging power, energy charged and electricity costs, plus monitoring of phase load at the house connection to prevent overloads. Visualised on a centrally placed monitor with a React front end.

datenschutz.title: Privacy Policy
datenschutz.hostingP1: This website is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany. The server location is Nuremberg, Germany. At the infrastructure level (network, hypervisor), Hetzner may process technical connection data. Information on this can be found in Hetzner's privacy policy: hetzner.com/de/legal/privacy-policy
datenschutz.hostingP2: As a reverse proxy, the server uses Traefik, managed via the deployment platform Coolify. For technical operation, Traefik may briefly process connection data such as IP addresses. These are not stored permanently and serve solely to provide the website and ensure its operational security. The Nuxt application itself writes no access logs and stores no personal usage data.
datenschutz.cookiesP1: This website uses no cookies and transmits no data to third-party providers such as Google Analytics or similar services.
datenschutz.cookiesP2: For analytics we use the self-hosted, data-minimising software Umami. Umami works without cookies, without cross-device identifiers and without building personal profiles. Only anonymised usage data is collected (e.g. pages visited, approximate origin at country level, browser type used); it is not possible to draw conclusions about individual people, and the data does not leave our own server environment hosted in Germany. Your IP address is only processed briefly on the server side to recognise repeat visits and determine the approximate origin; it is not stored, but merely fed into a daily-changing, irreversible key value. The statistical data collected in this way is kept for a maximum of 14 months and then deleted. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in the statistical analysis and improvement of our offering pursuant to Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
datenschutz.cookiesP3: Since this website itself neither stores nor reads any cookies or other data on your device that are not strictly necessary for operating the site, no consent banner and no consent under § 25 TDDDG is required for this.
datenschutz.linksP1: The legal notice of this website contains links to unsplash.com to credit the photos used. When you click these links, your IP address and a referrer parameter are transmitted to Unsplash. We have no influence over this data processing. Unsplash privacy policy: unsplash.com/privacy
datenschutz.contactFormP1: When you use the contact form, I process the data you provide (first and last name, email address, optionally phone number, the selected intent and topic, and your message) in order to handle and answer your enquiry. In addition, the time and the version of the privacy notice you confirmed are logged so that your consent can be evidenced.
datenschutz.contactFormP2: The legal basis for enquiries aimed at a contractual or business relationship is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, and otherwise our legitimate interest in answering your enquiry pursuant to Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
datenschutz.contactFormP3: For the technical receipt and reliable delivery of the form message by email, I use a central delivery service I operate myself ("hommrich-hub"), running on the same server infrastructure hosted in Germany (Hetzner, see section 2). The actual email dispatch is handled by the provider Brevo (Sendinblue GmbH), Köpenicker Straße 126, 10179 Berlin, Germany, acting as a processor on the basis of a contract pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. Brevo privacy policy: brevo.com/de/legal/privacypolicy
datenschutz.contactFormP4: Your details are used exclusively to handle your enquiry and are not used for advertising purposes. I delete the data as soon as your enquiry has been dealt with and no statutory retention obligations prevent this.
